slides.heading: Oral Lesson
bullets: In “Birds sing sweetly,” the word sweetly tells how the birds sing — it modifies the verb sing.
In “Very large vessels sailed,” the word very modifies the adjective large.
In “He rode quite fast,” the word quite modifies the adverb fast.
A word used to modify a verb, an adjective, or another adverb is called an Adverb.

slides.text: An Adverb is a word used to modify a verb, an adjective, a participle, or an adverb.

slides.heading: What Adverbs Tell
bullets: Adverbs usually tell how, when, where, or how much (to what degree).
How:  slowly, sweetly, well.   ·   When:  soon, now, yesterday.
Where:  here, there, near.   ·   How much:  very, quite, too.

slides.heading: Practice — Find the Adverb
slides.instruction: Name the adverb in each sentence.
items: You will never see him again.

slides.heading: Practice — What Does the Adverb Tell?
slides.instruction: Tell whether each adverb tells how, when, where, or how much.

slides.heading: Practice — What Does the Adverb Modify?
slides.instruction: Tell whether the adverb modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb.

slides.heading: Adverbial Element & Adverbial Clause
bullets: A word or group of words used like an adverb is an Adverbial Element.
When that group is a clause (it has its own subject and predicate), it is an Adverbial Clause.
“Flowers bloom when spring comes.” — “when spring comes” tells when they bloom.
Adverbial clauses begin with when, where, while, because, if, and many other words.

slides.heading: Practice — Find the Adverbial Clause
slides.instruction: Name the adverbial clause in each sentence.
items: We rested because we were tired.
Call me if you need help.
Plants grow where it is warm.

slides.heading: Common Mistakes with Adverbs
bullets: Don’t use two negatives:  “I don’t want anything,” not “I don’t want nothing.”
Use an -ly adverb to tell how you do something:  “drive safely,” not “drive safe.”
After looks, feels, smells, tastes, use an adjective:  “smells sweet,” not “smells sweetly.”
Say “I did well,” not “I did good.”

slides.heading: Practice — Fix the Adverb
slides.instruction: Each sentence has a mistake. Give the correct word.

items: Which is right: “drive safe” or “drive safely”?
answers: A word that modifies a verb, adjective, participle, or adverb.
How, when, where, or how much.
A word or group of words used like an adverb.
A clause used as an adverbial element.
When, where, while, because, if, and others.
